sections.heading: Signs It's Time to Look at Your Water Heater
body: Water heaters usually give a warning before they quit. Here's what to look for.

items.title: Water around the base
items.text: A puddle can come from a loose fitting or from the tank itself. If the tank is leaking, it can't be repaired and has to be replaced. Shut off the cold water to the heater and call.

items.title: No hot water, or not enough
items.text: A failed part is often a repair. A tank that can't keep up, after serving the house for a long time, may be ready to replace. We look at it before we say which.

items.title: Rusty or cloudy hot water
items.text: If the cold side runs clear and the hot side runs rusty, the problem is the heater. The inside of the tank may be corroding.

items.title: Rumbling or popping
items.text: Sediment settles at the bottom of the tank, and the heater makes noise as it heats. It can be a sign the tank is wearing out.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace?
body: Here's a rule you can check. If a part has failed and the tank is sound, repair makes sense. We repair and maintain most brands of water heaters.
If the tank itself is leaking, repair isn't an option. If the heater is old and the repairs keep coming, replacing it is usually the better use of your money.
We tell you which side of the line you're on. The quote is free either way.

sections.heading: Tank-Type or Tankless
body: We install both. Which one fits depends on your house, your family and what you want to spend. [[confirm: [X]-year warranty on our work]]

items.title: Tank-type
items.text: Stores and heats a tank of water so it's ready when you turn on the tap. It's the familiar choice, and it fits the setup most homes already have.

items.title: Tankless
items.text: Heats water as you use it instead of storing it. It can cost more to install, and your home may need venting or gas line changes, so we look at the house first.

items.title: Brands
items.text: Bradford White is our preferred brand. We also install AO Smith and Navien tankless water heaters.

sections.heading: Before You Call
body: If you can do it safely, shut off the cold water supply to the heater. Look around the base and the pipes for where the water is coming from, and take a photo or two.
Check the label for the brand and age, and tell us when you call. If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas company before anything else.

items.q: Does it cost anything to get a quote?
items.a: No, quotes are free. Tell us what you see and we'll tell you what we think.
Bradford White is our preferred brand. We also install AO Smith and Navien tankless water heaters, and we repair and maintain most brands.

items.q: Do you remove the old water heater?
items.a: Ask when you call, and ask for it to be written into the quote. You should know what the price covers before the work starts.

items.q: How long does a replacement take?
items.a: It depends on the heater and the house. Tell us what you have and we'll tell you what to expect, and ask for the time window on the phone.
Call and ask. The office is open Monday to Friday, 7:30 AM to 4:30 PM, so call early in the day and we'll work out a time.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong With a Toilet
body: Most toilet problems come down to a short list of parts.

items.title: A toilet that keeps running
items.text: Usually the flapper or the fill valve inside the tank. They're small parts, and a running toilet wastes water all day.

items.title: Water at the base
items.text: A worn wax ring or loose bolts can let water out at the floor. It can leak slowly and damage the floor before you see it, so don't wait.

items.title: A weak or incomplete flush
items.text: Often a partial clog, or a tank that isn't filling the way it should.

items.title: A toilet that rocks
items.text: A loose toilet is a seal problem waiting to happen. It should sit solid on the floor.

items.title: A crack in the bowl or tank
items.text: A cracked fixture leaks, and it isn't something to patch. That one is a replacement.

sections.heading: Clogs and Slow Drains
body: A toilet that clogs once is a plunger problem. A toilet that clogs again and again may have a blockage further down the line, and plunging harder won't fix that.
Tell us how often it happens and whether other drains in the house are slow. That tells us where to look.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace?
body: Here's a rule you can check. If it's a flapper, a fill valve or a wax ring, repair is the answer, and it costs far less than a new toilet.
If the bowl or tank is cracked, or the toilet has needed repair after repair, a new one is usually the better use of your money.
We tell you which side of the line you're on, and the quote is free either way.

We work on any brand, old or new. If we find something behind the toilet that changes the job, you'll hear about it before the work goes further.
